conflict_synopsis.core_view: Post-hike US 2s10s flattening prices a growth scare that hard activity, tight credit and low vol do not confirm, so the curve should steepen.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Expansionary US activity/labor prints after a fully priced 25bp hike, against a 1y-extreme 25bp 2s10s.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: Labor and surveys break weaker with HY/VIX stress while 2s10s keeps flattening.

remit: strongest pro-growth, risk-on or cyclical macro expression
stance_summary: Post-hike recession flattening is over-discounted: hard activity, credit and vol still look expansionary, so the cleanest pro-growth expression is a duration-neutral US 2s10s steepener rather than stretched cyclical FX.

catalysts: US activity and labor prints that stay expansionary versus a curve that already flattened 21bp in a month
August retail +1.2% feeding into spending and reducing the consumer-scare read from Michigan 47.8
Canada activity/energy pass-through keeping North American term premium from collapsing even if the Fed is done for this meeting
NZ GDP beat and India FTA as global cyclical confirmation, expressed here via the US curve rather than NZD because NZ yields are unavailable
evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact
rollup:New Zealand Q2 GDP slows to 0.2% q/q but beats forecasts
rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Duration-neutral US 2s10s steepener: receive UST 2Y versus pay UST 10Y. Packet print is 25bp on 2026-09-18, 1y percentile 0.2% / z_1y -2.45 after a -21bp 1m flatten (z -2.20). Alternative considered: long CA-US 5Y (pay CA 5Y / receive US 5Y) at -124bp, 1y percentile 0.2% and 5y percentile 6.9%.
expression_comparison.rationale: Rates are preferred because the growth-versus-recession discrepancy lives in curve shape, not in a cheap FX level. US 2s10s owns that gap directly after a fully priced 25bp hike, while NZDUSD mixes an energy-importer shock, unavailable NZ yields, and weak NZ labor (47.0). USDCAD is inferior because the packet's USDCAD vs CA-US 2Y residual is weak (r-squared 0.022) and 140bp 2Y carry favors USD over CAD. CA-US 5Y is a strong RV but is closer to the existing 150-175bp policy-rate gap (Fed 3.75-4.00% vs BoC 2.25%) than to a growth mispricing. NZ-involved rate RV is unavailable.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Long NZDUSD (spot 0.5711, 5y percentile 8.6%, -3.90% 1m) as the cheapest cyclical USD pair after NZ Q2 GDP +0.2% q/q beat forecasts; runner-up short USDCAD on Canada activity 53.2 versus US 49.92.

trade.horizon: 4-8 weeks; post-hike data and next inflation/labor prints to test whether the 1m flatten was a growth scare or a completed hiking event
trade.invalidation: ISM Services or manufacturing fall into contraction, payrolls and unemployment break materially weaker, and HY OAS/VIX reprice a growth accident while 2s10s keeps flattening. A 5y-window confirmation that 25bp is a normal curve in this hiking regime without a growth rebound would also downgrade the stretch argument.
trade.mispricing: US 2s10s at 25bp (1y percentile 0.2%, 1m -21bp) prices a hiking-into-slowdown path that is not confirmed by expansionary ISM services, stable labor, tight HY, low VIX, or high copper. The 5y 2s10s percentile of 54% means this is a change/1y-distribution discrepancy, not a 5y cheapness claim. Credit-equity-survey triangulation says the recession flattening overshot.
principal_risks: Energy shock absorbers weaken further and a genuine stagflation hit validates the flatten; BoC already flags fuel pass-through and Shell/Equinor warn buffers are thinner.
US consumer remains the soft spot: temperature 48.5, Michigan preliminary September 47.8 (-7.5% m/m), Q2 GDP +1.5% SAAR versus +2.1% in Q1.
The 5y 2s10s percentile is 54%, so 1y-window extremes can persist if this hiking regime has a lower curve mean; mean reversion is a yardstick, not the signal.
Another hawkish Fed or upside CPI surprise can extend bear-flattening if 2Y cheapens faster than 10Y; August CPI already kept the tightening bias intact.

Australian housing (stamp duty -24% y/y, prices more than 7% off peak) is a real regional growth hole; this trade does not own that, but a broader commodity risk-off could still flatten UST via a global scare.
Positioning, dealer balance sheet and executable levels are unknown; paper books are empty and Cot/flow is a known gap.
trade.structure: Duration-neutral 2s10s steepener: receive US 2Y versus pay US 10Y. Equal-yield weights are not claimed; packet notes 2s5s10s is equal-yield, not DV01-neutral. No executable structure or size is in the packet.
trade.thesis: FACT: The Fed delivered the widely priced 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%; futures had assigned greater than 90% odds before the meeting. US 2Y is 4.76% (1y percentile 99.8%, +57bp 1m) and US 10Y is 5.01% (1y percentile 99.6%, +36bp 1m), leaving 2s10s at 25bp. That spread's 252-observation percentile is 0.0 with z -2.49, 1y percentile 0.2% / z_1y -2.45, and a -21bp 1m change (z -2.20); 5s10s is 15bp with 1y percentile 0.4%. FACT: Hard US data are not collapsing. Unemployment is 4.1% unchanged; payrolls +162k with positive revisions; ISM Services 55.4 with business activity and new orders above 60; ISM Manufacturing 54.6 still expansionary; August retail sales +1.2% m/m after July was revised to -0.5%. FACT: Risk markets are not pricing a growth accident: VIX 15.44 (14.7th percentile), HY OAS 270bp (13.7th percentile), S&P 500 7638 (90th percentile, +1.13% 1d), copper 6.59 (92nd percentile). Canada Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q and activity temperature 53.2 are the strongest cyclical prints in the four-country set; NZ Q2 GDP +0.2% q/q beat forecasts. INFERENCE: The 1m bear-flattening is the market's slowdown tax on a hike that was already in the price. If growth and risk appetite remain resilient, 2s should stop cheapening versus 10s: either the additional-hike premium in 2s fades now that September is delivered, or term yields stay bid with activity and the curve re-steepens. The desk line that domestic growth is softer is the over-discounted pessimism. UNKNOWN: Next-meeting hike odds are not in the packet; positioning/flow is unavailable; NZ yields are blocked so NZ growth cannot be expressed in rates; 5y 2s10s percentile is 54%, so the flattening is extreme only on the 1y window.
why_now: The Sep 16 hike is done and had been greater than 90% priced, so further flattening now has to come from a genuine growth scare rather than from delivering a known FOMC outcome.
US 2s10s just printed the 0th percentile of the 252-observation opportunity screen and 1y percentile 0.2% after a statistically large 1m flatten.
Same-week triangulation is still expansionary: ISM Services 55.4, August retail +1.2%, payrolls +162k, VIX 15.44, HY OAS 270bp, copper at the 92nd percentile.
Canada and NZ growth prints (CA GDP +0.8% q/q; NZ GDP beat at +0.2% q/q) argue the global cyclical complex is not rolling over even as the desk narrative leans softer growth.
Saudi ship-to-ship workaround and modest oil easing reduce the extreme left tail that would justify a lasting curve collapse, even though energy shock absorbers remain a risk.
